summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of orthotopic liver transplant, recurrent urinary tract infections, and urinary retention requiring an indwelling catheter, was admitted for treatment of a positive urine culture with multidrug-resistant organisms, including Pseudomonas. Although largely asymptomatic, due to his immunocompromised state and prior urosepsis, the infectious disease team recommended a five-day course of IV meropenem to eradicate potential colonizing bacteria. The Foley catheter was removed upon admission, and the patient successfully voided without difficulty. A prostate ultrasound showed no abscess. Repeat urine culture after treatment showed no growth. The patient was discharged on a regimen of weekly fosfomycin for long-term suppression and instructed to monitor for urinary symptoms. He remained stable throughout the admission with no complications.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Pseudomonas infection in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site
Hypertrophy (benign) of prostate with urinary obstruction and other lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS)
Infection and inflammatory reaction due to indwelling urinary catheter
